title: Lior and the Rivergate
premise: Bush pilot Isandro Fairweather agrees to fly a dying prospector's map to the man's estranged daughter, only to discover the map points to the Rivergate — a legendary source of the interior's great river said to hold water that preserves memory itself. Racing the dry season and pursued by a mining consortium that wants the source dammed and its power monopolized, Isandro travels upstream with the daughter, Maren, falling for her even as duty demands he deliver her and turn back. At the Rivergate, Isandro must choose between drinking from waters that would return his lost memories — including why he fled the coast twelve years ago — or destroying the gate to keep it out of the consortium's hands. He shatters it, losing his own chance at restoration but gaining a future with Maren, as the river runs free and the secret dies with the season.
about_author: Dominic Voss is a former bush pilot turned novelist who spent six years flying supply runs across remote river country before trading his logbook for a manuscript. He writes adventure fiction about people who measure their lives in miles, drawing on real maps, real weather, and the rumors pilots trade over bad coffee.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior establishes his solitary life, his battered plane the Kestrel, and the rumor economy of frontier strips. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness masking an old wound he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isandro finds old Tobin Hale collapsed at a remote strip, gold-dust fevered and dying. Tobin trades a hand-drawn map for a promise: carry it to his daughter in Merrow's Landing. Isandro accepts, uneasy. Beat: obligation taking root before he understands its weight.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Alone at night, Isandro studies the map and realizes it marks the Rivergate — the forbidden source every pilot jokes about and no one claims to have seen. A consortium survey plane shadows him overhead. Beat: wonder curdling into danger.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In Merrow's Landing, Maren Hale receives Isandro and the map, furious at the father who abandoned her, hungry for the truth he never gave. She decides she's going upstream whether anyone flies her or not. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Dry Season Countdown
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The consortium's agent, Corvus Renner, offers Isandro a fortune to hand over the map; refusal means his fuel contracts vanish. With the dry season closing low-water windows on the river, they must leave now. Beat: duty versus survival.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: The flight upriver through storm cells and unmapped ridges; Maren proves fearless, and banter becomes trust. They crash-land on a gravel bar when the Kestrel's engine ingests grit. Beat: first bond forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Wrecked World Below
chapters.summary: Stranded, they salvage supplies and meet river trader Odile Brant, who ferries them by barge and tells stories of the Gate — including that those who drink remember everything, even what others paid to forget. Beat: temptation introduced.

chapters.title: Renner's Net
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. The consortium closes the river: checkpoints, bribed guides, a bounty. Renner is revealed as a former prospector whose memories were taken at the Gate and sold. Beat: villain given a wound, not just a want.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Shooting the Serrated Reach by canoe, Maren nearly drowns; Isandro saves her and, shaking, admits he once lost someone because he chose duty over love. Beat: intimacy through shared peril and confession.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgets
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A riverside village where elders drink diluted Gate water ceremonially, holding centuries of memory between them. They warn: the Gate gives back everything, including guilt. Maren learns her father visited here years ago. Beat: awe shadowed by warning.

chapters.title: Tobin's Trail
chapters.summary: Following Tobin's old markings, they find his abandoned camp and journals revealing he drank from the Gate, saw his whole life, and still walked away from Maren — out of shame, not indifference. Beat: forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Fork
chapters.summary: Renner's hired men strike at the river fork; Odile sacrifices her barge to cover their escape up the wrong channel. Isandro takes a bullet graze. Beat: cost made real, allies spent.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Whispers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Portaging a gorge where wind through stone mimics voices from the past; Isandro hears his lost sister's voice and nearly turns back alone. Maren anchors him. Beat: love against the gravity of memory.

chapters.title: Renner Catches Up
chapters.summary: Renner confronts them personally, offering Maren her father's full memories — which he bought from the Gate decades ago — in exchange for safe passage. Maren wavers; Isandro cannot decide for her. Beat: moral stakes sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: What Maren Chose
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Alone with Renner's offer, Maren reads Tobin's final letter and chooses the living future over the recorded past, rejecting the deal. Renner, enraged, forces them ahead as guides to the Gate. Beat: agency claimed.

chapters.title: The Last Water
chapters.summary: Forced march through dying tributaries as the dry season bites; Renner's men mutiny, and Isandro quietly sabotages the expedition's radio. A fragile truce forms between hunter and hunted. Beat: enemies bound by the same thirst.

chapters.title: The Rivergate
chapters.summary: They reach the source: a spring-fed basin where the river rises whole from the earth, water impossibly clear, the air thick with remembered voices. Renner drinks and collapses into total recall. Beat: transcendence and terror at once.

chapters.title: Everything I Ever Was
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the water's edge, Isandro faces his own memories — the sister he failed, the promise he broke. Drinking would restore him whole; he kneels at the brink. Beat: climax of the internal war.

chapters.title: Breaking the Gate
chapters.summary: Climax. Renner, restored and ruthless, moves to claim the source for the consortium. Isandro detonates the rock shelf sealing the spring, collapsing the basin into the aquifer — destroying the Gate forever, with Maren's help pulling him clear. Beat: sacrifice over salvation.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The long journey down a changed river; Renner, hollowed by what he remembers, lets them go. Maren scatters Tobin's ashes at the village that forgot him, and the elders remember him aloud one last time. Beat: grief transmuted into peace.

chapters.title: Merrow's Landing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Repairs, reckonings, and a rebuilt Kestrel. Isandro chooses to stay grounded long enough to build something instead of outrunning it; he and Maren commit to each other without promises of permanence — only presence. Beat: love chosen freely.

chapters.title: The River Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Epilogue. A year later, Isandro flies medicine runs again, Maren mapping the watershed for the villages. The Gate is rumor again, and this time no map leads to it. Final beat: a life measured in miles that finally has somewhere to land.
